title: 1978 AHSME Problem 15
statement: If \(\sin x+\cos x=\frac15\) and \(0\le x\lt\pi,\) then \(\tan x\) is

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: not completely determined by the given information

solutions.text:
Squaring gives \(1+2\sin x\cos x=\frac{1}{25},\) so \(\sin x\cos x=-\frac{12}{25}.\) Thus \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\) are the roots of \[ t^2-\frac15t-\frac{12}{25}=0, \] namely \(\frac{4}{5}\) and \(-\frac{3}{5}.\) Because \(\sin x\ge0\) on the given interval, \(\sin x=\frac{4}{5}\) and \(\cos x=-\frac{3}{5}.\) Hence \(\tan x=-\frac{4}{3}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Square the given equation to determine \(\sin x\cos x\)
Treat \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\) as roots of a quadratic, then use \(0\le x\lt\pi\)
